summary.headline: JNK India Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 80.6% YoY to INR 186 crore; EBITDA margin 11.8% after Chemdist losses, PAT up 8.5x to INR 9.6 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 80.6% YoY to INR 186 crore and EBITDA rose 3.1x to INR 21.9 crore, with margin at 11.8% versus 7% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA margin was 14%, with the gap explained by an operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore at the JNK Chemdist JV. Order book stood at INR 1,801 crore as of 30 June 2026, and FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth and 12-14% EBITDA margin was reiterated. An export order received on 8 June 2026 was cancelled before any costs were incurred, due to licensor technical approval not materialising.

segments.name: Heating equipment (core)
segments.commentary: About 60% of the current opportunity pipeline; management targets heating at about 60% of revenue in the medium term. Export bids (about INR 3,000 crore) are mainly heating, largely routed through JNK Global.

segments.name: Non-heating / adjacencies (process plants, metals & minerals, offshore, renewables)
segments.commentary: About 40% of pipeline, with domestic bids of INR 3,000-plus crore. Target is about 40% of revenue from non-heating within 3-5 years; hit rate expected 10-12% initially versus 20-25% in heating.

segments.name: JNK Chemdist Technologies (JV)
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.8% of group revenue in Q1 FY27 with an operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore on high fixed costs. Guided to 10-15% of JNK India revenue and about 20% gross margin; expected to turn profitable by year-end. Current green hydrogen orders about INR 50 crore.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of about 20-25% for FY27 maintained.
Full-year EBITDA margin guidance of about 12-14% maintained; management said there is no change, though the company later said it would recheck the figures it had announced.
Pipeline of more than INR 6,000 crore (about 50:50 export and domestic); management expects these bids to be finalised in FY27 with a hit rate of 20-25% in heating.
Refinery and fertiliser order finalisation expected in Q2-Q3 FY27.
BPCL Bina execution to occur uniformly in FY27 and FY28; EBITDA in line with guidance.
Chemdist expected to be EBITDA-positive by year-end FY27 (full year, not a specific quarter).
capex_capacity: Unbilled revenue at end-Q1 about INR 200-221 crore following shift to input-method revenue recognition.
Company has board approval to register a branch office in Iraq; no physical setup yet and an agent is in place.
Non-fund-based (bank guarantee) limit enhancement may be needed for new contracts; no significant debt raising expected in the next 4-6 quarters, per management.
Revenue seasonality: Q1 is 10-15% of full-year revenue, H1 30-35%, H2 60-70%.
demand_pricing: Order book INR 1,801 crore at 30 June 2026; pipeline above INR 6,000 crore, up from about INR 4,000 crore previously.
Export pipeline about INR 3,000 crore, mainly Africa (Nigeria, Ethiopia) and Middle East; Dangote Phase 2 under discussion, described as a likely repeat order.
Non-heating TAM in India cited as USD 300-500 million (offshore) and USD 500 million-1 billion (metals and minerals); target project size USD 30-60 million, up to about INR 1,000-2,000 crore.
Commodity prices fluctuating; management said ongoing projects are costed and sub-vendor orders placed on fixed-price basis, so no major margin impact.
Working capital: large customers (Reliance, private companies, BPCL Bina) have friendly payment terms; JNK Global bank guarantees on back-to-back export orders.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term revenue target beyond FY27 and capacity to ramp non-heating business?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth of 20-25% annually; non-heating to reach about 40% of revenue in 3-5 years. Management said diversification will not ramp within 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export order cancelled and what has been done to prevent recurrence?
qa_highlights.answer: Cancelled due to end-user licensor technical approval not materialising; EPC contractor was confident, and no costs had been incurred. The licensor has since qualified JNK for future projects but not ongoing ones. SOPs being tightened.

qa_highlights.question: Margin decline in Q1 despite gross margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Chemdist operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore; standalone EBITDA margin was 14% on lower Q1 revenue of about INR 170 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Hit rate and TAM in new non-heating segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected hit rate of about 10-12% initially versus 20-25% in heating; target bids of USD 30-60 million, and EBITDA margin in line with 12-14% guidance.

qa_highlights.question: JNK Global cooperation agreement renewal (3-year term in DRHP)?
qa_highlights.answer: Not formally renewed yet; management believes it is in force or continues automatically, with no change in terms.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue and accounting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue recognition moved from output to input method; unbilled revenue about INR 200-221 crore at end Q1. Management said working capital cycle is unchanged as customer payment schedules are unchanged.

risks_watch: Export order cancellation (8 June 2026 order) shows licensor approval risk on international EPC contracts.
Chemdist JV losses until break-even; management expects year-end profitability but gave no quarterly guidance.

Unclear reconciliation of EBITDA guidance (12-14% now vs 14-15% previously cited by an analyst) and corrections to the presentation, including a revised filing for standalone profit-after-tax margin rows.
Lower hit rate and new technology qualification risk in non-heating businesses; reliance on technology partners.
Governance: activist dispute at JNK Global (sub judice) and status of the JNK Global cooperation agreement, which is not formally renewed.
Revenue seasonality and back-ended recognition; unbilled revenue of about INR 200 crore to watch.
Bank guarantee limit enhancement may be needed for new contracts; Dangote Phase 2 award pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the order pipeline and margins, but defensive on the cancellation, the JNK Global governance dispute and guidance inconsistencies, which management declined to comment on or said it would recheck. Several answers were deferred to follow-up or to the filings.
